topic: Hotspot Row Locks Kill High-Volume Writes
postText:
Your database has optimal composite indexes. Query plans show index seeks. Memory and CPU sit comfortably below 40%. Yet under morning peak traffic, transactions grind to complete standstill with cascading lock timeouts and 40001 serialization errors.

Here is what happens in healthcare IT when hundreds of clinical workflows claim bed spaces or allocate limited medication lots simultaneously: every transaction issues `UPDATE stock SET qty = qty - 1 WHERE item_id = ?`.

Even with cluster primary key lookups, row-level exclusive locks (X-locks) queue sequentially. Transaction execution time jumps from 2ms to 600ms due to lock-wait saturation. Connection pools exhaust. App workers hang.

We solved this hotspot bottleneck without external caching layers by shifting row mutations into two architectural patterns:

1. Sharded Counter Slots: Split single hot record into N internal slot rows (e.g., item_101_slot_0 through slot_9). Writes update a random slot using `CRC32(tx_id) % N`, eliminating row lock contention. Read totals simply aggregate `SUM(qty)`.

2. Append-Only Deltas: Replace row updates with raw append-only ledger entries (`+1`, `-1`). Asynchronous background jobs aggregate ledger rows into master balances using `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.

Stop forcing relational engines to serialize high-concurrency updates on singleton records.

How does your team handle high-concurrency balance or inventory updates? Do you partition counters, rely on distributed Redis locks, or stream deltas through Kafka?
